# OM System (Olympus)

## Brand Overview

OM System (spun off from Olympus in 2021 as OM Digital Solutions) is a Micro Four Thirds-only manufacturer. Known for compact, weather-sealed, lightweight bodies with pro-grade IP53 weather sealing on higher-end models. OM System delivers industry-leading IBIS (up to 8.5 stops on the OM-1 II). The MFT lens mount is shared with Panasonic, giving access to a massive shared lens ecosystem of 100+ lenses. The 2x crop factor means the lightest possible lenses for any given field of view among interchangeable lens cameras -- physically smaller sensor elements, shorter flange distances, and smaller glass all compound into dramatic weight savings. A complete OM System portrait kit can weigh less than a single full-frame body.

**Notes:**
- **OM-1 Mark II** -- The flagship. Stacked sensor enables 50 fps with full AF/AE tracking and 120 fps with fixed AF -- unmatched in MFT for capturing fleeting expressions. AI-based human detection AF, cross-quad pixel PDAF with 1053 points. Best EVF in the system. Dual SD slots. At 599g it is lighter than any full-frame flagship by a wide margin.
- **OM-5** -- The compact enthusiast choice. Same 20 MP sensor as the OM-1 in a smaller body. IP53 weather sealing, excellent 6.5-stop IBIS (7.5 with Sync IS lenses). 30 fps electronic burst with Pro Capture mode. Single SD slot. Battery life is modest; carry a spare.
- **E-M10 Mark IV** -- The budget lightweight. 383g with battery. Contrast-detect AF (121 points) is capable but a step behind the phase-detect systems above. Flip-down selfie LCD. No weather sealing. Best value entry into MFT for portraits on a budget.
- **PEN E-P7** -- The ultra-compact rangefinder-style body at just 337g. No EVF (LCD only), which keeps it tiny. Same sensor/processor as the E-M10 IV. Not officially sold in North America (import only). No weather sealing. Ideal as a second body or for discreet street/portrait work.

## Lens Recommendations

### Prime Lenses (all MFT, 2x crop)

**35mm equiv:** Olympus M.Zuiko 17mm f/1.8 (tiny, affordable) or 17mm f/1.2 PRO (weather sealed, premium rendering, 390g). The f/1.8 is the lightweight pick; the f/1.2 PRO delivers superior bokeh and build.

**50mm equiv:** Olympus M.Zuiko 25mm f/1.8 (137g, a featherweight normal prime) or 25mm f/1.2 PRO (weather sealed, creamy bokeh, 410g). The f/1.2 PRO is the portrait standout -- tack sharp wide open with exceptional subject rendering.

**85mm equiv:** Olympus M.Zuiko 45mm f/1.8 (116g, legendary value) or 45mm f/1.2 PRO (weather sealed, 410g, the ultimate MFT portrait lens). The 45mm f/1.8 at 116g is one of the lightest portrait-length lenses ever made for any system.

### Zoom Lenses (24-80mm equiv)

- **Olympus M.Zuiko 12-40mm f/2.8 PRO II** -- The standard pro zoom. Constant f/2.8, IP53 weather sealed, fluorine coated, 382g. Covers 24-80mm equiv. MF clutch. The workhorse.
- **Olympus M.Zuiko 12-45mm f/4 PRO** -- Ultra-compact alternative at just 254g. Constant f/4, weather sealed, outstanding macro (0.5x equiv). One stop slower but dramatically lighter. Covers 24-90mm equiv.

## System Weight Examples

MFT is the lightest interchangeable-lens system available. These kits are substantially lighter than any APS-C or full-frame equivalent.

**Kit 1: Ultra-Light Portrait Kit**
- E-M10 IV body (383g) + 45mm f/1.8 (116g) = **499g total**
- FF equivalent: 90mm f/1.8 portrait lens on a body. A comparable Sony A7C II + 85mm f/1.8 = 1,043g. This MFT kit is less than half the weight.

**Kit 2: Two-Prime Portrait Kit**
- OM-5 body (414g) + 25mm f/1.8 (137g) + 45mm f/1.8 (116g) = **667g total**
- Two portrait-length primes (50mm + 90mm equiv) in a weather-sealed body, for less than the weight of most full-frame bodies alone.

**Kit 3: Pro Portrait Kit**
- OM-1 II body (599g) + 45mm f/1.2 PRO (410g) + 12-40mm f/2.8 PRO II (382g) = **1,391g total**
- A flagship body, the best MFT portrait prime, and a pro zoom covering 24-80mm. A comparable Canon R5 II + RF 85mm f/1.2L + RF 24-70mm f/2.8L = 3,090g. The OM System kit is 55% lighter while delivering pro-grade weather sealing and burst performance.

## Key Strengths and Weaknesses

**Strengths:**
- **Weight (lightest system)** -- MFT's 2x crop means the smallest lenses for any given focal length. Complete kits can weigh under 500g. No other ILC system comes close.
- **Weather sealing (best in class)** -- IP53-rated bodies and PRO lenses. Shoot in rain, dust, and freezing conditions with confidence.
- **IBIS (best in class)** -- Up to 8.5 stops on the OM-1 II. Handheld shots at absurdly slow shutter speeds. High-Res Shot mode delivers 50-80 MP handheld composites.
- **Huge MFT lens ecosystem** -- Shared mount with Panasonic means 100+ native lenses. Every focal length and price point is covered, from budget primes to premium f/1.2 glass.

**Weaknesses:**
- **Smallest sensor = most noise at high ISO** -- The MFT sensor is roughly 2 stops behind full frame in high-ISO noise performance. Indoor portraits at ISO 3200+ will show more grain than FF or APS-C equivalents. The stacked sensor in the OM-1 II helps, but physics is physics.
- **Depth of field limitation** -- The 2x crop factor applies to DoF equivalence: 45mm f/1.2 on MFT provides the field of view of 90mm but the depth of field equivalent to roughly 90mm f/2.4 on full frame. You cannot achieve the razor-thin separation of an 85mm f/1.4 on FF.
- **Brand uncertainty** -- The Olympus divestiture to Japan Industrial Partners (2021) and rebranding to OM System raised long-term viability questions. Product releases have continued (OM-1 II, OM-5, new lenses) but the cadence is slower than Sony/Canon/Fuji. The lens roadmap is less aggressive.
